name: asyncio anyio task groups cancellation
short_definition: Structured concurrency for Python services: prefer task groups and cancel scopes (asyncio.TaskGroup and/or anyio) so child tasks cannot outlive parents, cancellations propagate predictably, and timeouts use fail_after/move_on_after or asyncio.timeout — avoiding fire-and-forget create_task leaks.
scope_in: asyncio event loop model; asyncio.TaskGroup; anyio create_task_group cancel scopes fail_after move_on_after shield get_cancelled_exc_class; to_thread.run_sync for blocking I/O; cancellation hygiene (reraise cancel exceptions); FastAPI async route concurrency; httpx.AsyncClient lifecycle; nursery-style pipelines; capacity limits.
scope_out: Worker job frameworks (Celery/arq/Temporal — see workers cluster); free-threading GIL details (py-versions); full Trio-only apps; multiprocessing; UI async; GPU kernels.
defaults: Async by default for I/O-bound FastAPI/services. Use anyio.create_task_group (or asyncio.TaskGroup on 3.11+) for concurrent child work that must complete or cancel together. Timeouts: anyio.fail_after / asyncio.timeout around external calls. HTTP: one httpx.AsyncClient per app lifespan, not per request. Blocking CPU/disk: anyio.to_thread.run_sync (or asyncio.to_thread) with limits — never block the event loop. Always reraise cancellation exceptions after cleanup; use shielded scopes for short finalizers. Prefer anyio APIs in libraries that might run under Trio or need cancel-scope semantics. FastAPI routes: async def for I/O; def only for trivial sync CPU. Structured logging with request_id across tasks.
decision_gates: USE task groups when: fan-out I/O (parallel fetches), background work scoped to a request/lifespan, pipelines that must not leak tasks. USE plain await when: single sequential I/O chain. DO NOT use asyncio.create_task without storing/awaiting or supervising — only for carefully documented process-level daemons with shutdown hooks. Prefer anyio when: need cancel scopes, fail_after, backend neutrality, or thread cancel checks. Prefer asyncio.TaskGroup when: stdlib-only constraint and Python ≥3.11. Hand off to processes/Rust when: CPU-bound multi-second work that would need a process pool anyway.
do_dont: DO: async with create_task_group() as tg: tg.start_soon(...); set timeouts on every network call; close clients in lifespan; catch get_cancelled_exc_class() only to cleanup then raise; use CapacityLimiter for thread offload; test cancellation paths. DON'T: fire-and-forget create_task for request work; swallow CancelledError/BaseException; time.sleep in async functions; run heavy CPU on the loop; nest task groups across async generators unsafely; cancel and ignore shielded cleanup failures silently forever; mix blocking Supabase/sync SDK calls on the loop without to_thread.
code_skeleton:
import anyio
from anyio import create_task_group, fail_after, get_cancelled_exc_class

async def fetch_one(client, url: str) -> bytes:
    with fail_after(5):
        # client is httpx.AsyncClient from lifespan
        resp = await client.get(url)
        resp.raise_for_status()
        return resp.content

async def fetch_many(client, urls: list[str]) -> list[bytes]:
    results: list[bytes | None] = [None] * len(urls)

    async def worker(i: int, url: str) -> None:
        results[i] = await fetch_one(client, url)

    async with create_task_group() as tg:
        for i, url in enumerate(urls):
            tg.start_soon(worker, i, url)
    return [r for r in results if r is not None]

async def with_cleanup(resource) -> None:
    try:
        await resource.work()
    except get_cancelled_exc_class():
        with anyio.CancelScope(shield=True):
            await resource.aclose()
        raise
failure_modes: 1) Orphan tasks after response returns (create_task without join). 2) Event loop blocked by sync I/O → latency cliffs. 3) Swallowed CancelledError → shutdown hangs. 4) Missing timeouts → stuck connections. 5) Shared non-thread-safe state across tasks without locks. 6) httpx client created per request → socket exhaustion. 7) TaskGroup exception groups obscure root cause if not logged. 8) Cancel scope stack corruption via yield inside task group in async generators. 9) Thread work ignoring from_thread.check_cancelled. 10) Deadlock: task A waits B while B waits A inside same group misuse.
anti_patterns: asyncio.ensure_future / create_task without supervision for business work; while True: await sleep without cancellation/backpressure; nesting asyncio.run inside running loop; global mutable dicts as caches without coordination; time.sleep; requests (sync) inside async routes; bare except Exception that eats cancellation (on some versions CancelledError bases changed — still never bare-except); infinite gather without return_exceptions planning; spawning tasks in __init__ of request-scoped objects.
tools: Primary: anyio (task groups, cancel scopes, to_thread), asyncio stdlib (TaskGroup, timeout, Event). HTTP: httpx.AsyncClient. Server: uvicorn/granian. Testing: pytest-anyio or pytest-asyncio. Observability: OTel async instrumentation, structlog bind contextvars. Alternatives: Trio (anyio-compatible mindset), trio-asyncio bridges — not default for FastAPI.
versions_as_of: as_of 2026-07-13: anyio 4.x (docs 4.14.1 series); Python 3.12+ recommended (TaskGroup since 3.11, asyncio.timeout 3.11+). FastAPI async stack on anyio under Starlette. Pin anyio>=4.8,<5 when used directly; transitive via httpx/starlette often present.

deprecation_watch: asyncio.timeouts patterns pre-3.11 custom hacks; nest_asyncio in production; concurrent.futures as the only concurrency for I/O services; aiohttp as default client when httpx is stack standard (unless required); @asyncio.coroutine / yield-from era code; creating event loops manually in FastAPI workers.
ts_boundary: Next.js/TS BFF uses Promise.all / AbortSignal for structured cancellation analogs. When calling Python services: set HTTP client timeouts and abort on client disconnect where supported (SSE). Do not assume Python continues heavy work after client abort unless job is enqueued. Mirror timeout budgets: gateway < BFF < Python upstream.
rust_boundary: Hand off to Rust/Tokio when: millions of connections, multi-threaded async CPU+IO hybrids, or existing Axum mesh. Python anyio is fine for AI/IO orchestration. Prefer message queues between Python and Rust for long work rather than holding HTTP open.
supabase_boundary: Prefer asyncpg/SQLAlchemy async for DB from async routes. supabase-py may be sync in places — wrap with to_thread or use direct Postgres. Pool sizing must consider concurrent tasks (each task can hold a connection). Cancelled requests should not leave transactions open — use context managers and session cleanup in finally/shielded blocks.
boundary_contracts: OpenAPI operations document timeouts indirectly via SLOs; MCP tools must have hard fail_after budgets. Queue jobs: cancellation of HTTP does not cancel job — separate lifecycle. Propagate traceparent/request_id into start_soon tasks via contextvars copy.
decision_matrix_row: Problem: I/O concurrent orchestration in Python services → anyio task groups + asyncio. Problem: UI data fetching → TS Promise + AbortSignal. Problem: ultra-high concurrency gateways → Rust Tokio. Problem: multi-step durable agents → Temporal (not raw task groups).
threats: Resource exhaustion via unbounded task spawn; slowloris without timeouts; cancellation race leaving partial writes; thread pool saturation; context confusion if request-scoped credentials copied into long tasks; DoS by triggering expensive fan-out.
mitigations: Bound fan-out (semaphores/CapacityLimiter); timeouts everywhere; limit thread pool; do not start unsupervised tasks with user auth context for long work — enqueue instead; cancel scopes on request disconnect where framework supports; backpressure on queues; load tests for concurrency.
agent_codegen_policy: MUST: task groups for multi-child concurrency; timeouts on HTTP/DB; reraise cancellation; lifespan-managed clients; to_thread for sync SDKs. MUST NOT: create_task without await/supervisor for request work; time.sleep in async; swallow CancelledError; unbounded gather on user-controlled list sizes; sync requests library in async routes.
tests_required: Unit: fail_after raises TimeoutError; task group cancels siblings on child error; cancellation cleanup called. Integration: FastAPI route with parallel upstream mocks; lifespan client reuse. Load: optional concurrency smoke. pytest-anyio backends asyncio.
ci_gates: pytest async tests; ruff; basedpyright; optional banlist grep for time.sleep( in async modules and requests.get in async routes.
skill_scan_signals: POSITIVE: create_task_group, asyncio.TaskGroup, fail_after, asyncio.timeout, get_cancelled_exc_class, to_thread.run_sync, lifespan AsyncClient. NEGATIVE: asyncio.create_task without later await, time.sleep in async def, requests. in async routes, except Exception: pass around awaits, missing timeout on httpx calls.
skill_module_bullets:
- Structured concurrency: task groups, not fire-and-forget create_task.
- Timeouts on all external I/O (fail_after / asyncio.timeout).
- Always reraise cancellation after shielded cleanup.
- Lifespan-scoped httpx.AsyncClient.
- Offload blocking calls with to_thread + limits.
- anyio preferred for cancel-scope ergonomics in services/libraries.
- Bound fan-out; no user-controlled unbounded gather.

conflicts_noted: asyncio.TaskGroup vs anyio.create_task_group: anyio uses level cancellation (Trio-like); asyncio edge cancellation can surprise. Prefer anyio in new service libraries. Starlette/FastAPI already depend on anyio — using it is not exotic. Some guides still teach gather+create_task as primary pattern — treat as legacy for business logic.
